clue.text: Ratios accepted with gambles

parts.note: something accepted is in
to dice is to gamble, so gambles is dices

explanation.surface: A statistician notes the odds that were taken up by people placing bets.
explanation.definitionFit: Index numbers in economics and statistics are ratios against a base value, so indices can be read as ratios.

clue.text: Incestuous one left missing stigma

indicators.note: what is missing has been left out of the word, so those letters are struck from it

parts.note: incest keeps things in the family
the Roman numeral for one
the usual abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone guilty of incest who is left alone is marked with shame.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I and L from IN FAMILY and INFAMY remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Infamy is public disgrace or notoriety, the same mark of shame that a stigma carries.

clue.text: 11 in rebuilt side acknowledging personal terms?

definitions.note: a description of the thing, not a synonym

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another is placed inside it
something rebuilt is put together again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the number written as a Roman numeral, not a reference to the 11-across answer

explanation.surface: A cross-reference to another answer slotted into a reworked team, with a hint about personal terms.
explanation.walkthrough: In a puzzle full of cross-references, 11 looks like it points to MAID MARIAN; it is just eleven in Roman numerals. A team is a side of eleven, which adds to the trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Deixis is the linguistic term for words like I, you, here and now whose meaning depends on who is speaking, chiefly personal pronouns.

clue.text: 5 across expert rewrites Act 1, Sc. 1, to include Queen and Mark

indicators.note: including something means taking it inside, so the other pieces go into the reworked letters
a rewrite rearranges what was there, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: ACT with 1 as the Roman numeral I
SC with 1 as I
Elizabeth Regina
M is an abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: An expert rewrites the opening scene of a play to bring in a queen and a character called Mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 across is POTTING, so its expert is a potter. ER goes in after the first letter of the reworked letters, M after the third.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceramicist makes pottery, so is an expert at the craft of potting clay.

clue.text: Partisan's sound accom-paniment for Rosie (Lee)

indicators.note: sound tells us to go by how the word is spoken, not how it is spelt

parts.note: Cider with Rosie is the memoir by Laurie Lee, so cider goes with Rosie

explanation.surface: A partisan sound accompanying Rosie Lee, rhyming slang for a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosie Lee is Cockney rhyming slang for tea, which suggests something taken with tea; the brackets point instead to Laurie Lee's book Cider with Rosie.
explanation.definitionFit: A sider is one who takes a side, a partisan supporter of one party in a dispute.

clue.text: Too risqué in first half of game at the table?

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase standing for the activity carried on at a snooker table

indicators.note: one part is placed in the other, so it goes inside

parts.note: the first half of the game ping-pong
over the top, i.e. going too far

explanation.surface: A remark that's too risqué made halfway through a game of table tennis.
explanation.walkthrough: PING is the first half of ping-pong, itself a table game, which is why 'at the table' feels like it belongs to the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Potting is sinking balls into the pockets, which is what a player does at a snooker or billiard table.

clue.text: I'm employed in Italian restau-rant: see father's howler after bill's presented

indicators.note: after places the bird piece behind the bill piece in the answer's order

parts.note: PA is father, with the possessive S
a tab is a bill, as at a bar
an owl is a bird that hoots and howls in the night

explanation.surface: In a restaurant, a diner spots their father's blunder after the bill has arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken by the object itself. Howler suggests a gross mistake; here it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A pasta bowl is the dish an Italian restaurant serves spaghetti in, so it could fairly say it is employed there.

clue.text: See 9
Waits with eagerness, in charge of introduction

parts.note: one who waits with eagerness is agog
the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly awaiting the person in charge of making introductions.
explanation.definitionFit: Isagogic is a learned adjective meaning introductory, used especially of preliminary study of scripture.

clue.text: See 19
Not one of the L8, small time art crook disheartened, bagging only first of Utrillos

definitions.note: teasing: not one of the little green men (19, 8), but one of the Lincoln green men

indicators.note: to bag something is to put it inside a bag, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: the short form of Friday, a time of the week
taken as written

indicators.note: losing its heart leaves only the two outside letters of the word

parts.note: the initial of Utrillo, the French painter

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is wanted

parts.note: crook without its middle letters

explanation.surface: A petty art thief, losing heart, steals just one of Utrillo's paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: The L8 are the Lincoln green men, Robin Hood's band, dressed in Lincoln green; L is Lincoln throughout. ART and CK together bag the U.
explanation.definitionFit: Friar Tuck is the jovial priest of Robin Hood's outlaw band in Sherwood Forest, one of the merry men in Lincoln green.

clue.text: Profane abuse of seed box

indicators.note: abusing something mistreats it out of its proper shape, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
a crate is a wooden box

explanation.surface: Sacrilegious mistreatment of a seed box, as in a gardener's shed.
explanation.walkthrough: Profane looks like an adjective, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To profane something holy is to treat it with irreverence and violate its sanctity, which is to desecrate it.

clue.text: Not one of the L8, I am ordered to take in help and damage name

definitions.note: teasing: not one of the little green men (19, 8), but of the Lincoln green men

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside, so the other pieces go within
putting things in order rearranges them, so the letters are shuffled into a new sequence

parts.note: taken as written
aid is help
to mar is to damage
the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Someone ordered to help is asked to take on a task and ends up damaging a reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged MIA takes in AID and MAR, then N follows. The L8 are the Lincoln green men, Robin Hood's band; L stands for Lincoln throughout.
explanation.definitionFit: Maid Marian is Robin Hood's sweetheart in the legend, a companion of the outlaws of Sherwood rather than a merry man.

clue.text: Jill? Not the other one of the L8 before re-christening?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: not Jill but the other one of the nursery-rhyme pair, Jack, a pet form of this name

definitions.text: one of the L8 before re-christening?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: Little ... name before the outlaws jokingly reversed it

explanation.surface: Asking about Jill and whether one of a band had another name before being renamed.
explanation.walkthrough: The (4,6) answer is JOHN LITTLE, with LITTLE supplied by 19. Jack and Jill went up the hill; Jack is a familiar form of John. In the ballads the giant John Little was rechristened Little John.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack is the traditional nickname for anyone christened John, and John Little was Little John's original name in the Robin Hood ballads.

clue.text: Sir Bernard clearly enjoys a drink in the home of the L8!

parts.note: is not T, i.e. not teetotal; T stands for teetotal, as in TT
Sir Bernard Ingham, Margaret Thatcher's long-serving press secretary

explanation.surface: A famous Downing Street press secretary is evidently fond of a tipple.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as NOT T-INGHAM: an Ingham who is not teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nottingham is the city whose sheriff hunts Robin Hood, and nearby Sherwood Forest is where his band of outlaws lived.

clue.text: Unprejudiced 19 magazine watching p's and q's

definitions.note: the answer is used here as an adjective

parts.note: 19 is LITTLE, and Cosmo is the shortened title of Cosmopolitan magazine
minding your p's and q's means being careful to be well-mannered

explanation.surface: A glossy magazine that is open-minded and careful about its manners.
explanation.walkthrough: The 19 is a cross-reference to LITTLE, so a little magazine is a short form of its title.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmopolite is a citizen of the world, free from national or local prejudice; as an adjective it means broad-minded.

clue.text: Inaccessible quantity of water taken away by guide

parts.note: a sea is a large body of water
a guide leads people off, so someone taken away by one is led off

explanation.surface: A stretch of water that cannot be reached, and someone led away by a guide.
explanation.definitionFit: An area that has been sealed off is closed to entry, so nobody can get into it.

clue.text: Antony and Lester score, but not 21 — 19 change for Helmut!
Mountain climbing attached to rope that may be put down

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing reads upwards, so the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: an alp is a mountain
a cable is a thick rope

explanation.surface: A climber on a mountain is tied to a rope that could be laid down.
explanation.walkthrough: Put down here means quelled or calmed, as with anger, not set on the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone placable can be appeased or pacified, so their anger can be quelled or calmed.

clue.text: Not one of the L8, leaves vehicle allowance

definitions.note: teasing: not one of the little green men (19, 8), but of the Lincoln green men

parts.note: to leave something to an heir is to will it
a car is a vehicle
a let is an allowance or permission, as in to let someone do something

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a car and an allowance in their will.
explanation.walkthrough: Leaves looks like foliage or departing; it is the verb of bequeathing.
explanation.definitionFit: Will Scarlet is one of Robin Hood's merry men, so one of the outlaws clad in Lincoln green.

clue.text: Paradoxical beings from the big red planet?

definitions.text: Paradoxical beings from the big red planet?

parts.note: surface reading: beings whose description contradicts where they come from
setter's reading: Martians, popularly pictured as small and green although Mars is the large red planet

explanation.walkthrough: The paradox is the colour and size: the planet is big and red, its supposed inhabitants are small and green.
explanation.definitionFit: Popular science fiction pictures aliens, especially Martians, as tiny green humanoids, the stock phrase for extraterrestrials.

clue.text: Remove flaws from absolute corrupter

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ..., i.e. take the spots off
second meaning: an absolute ruler, the sort that absolute power corrupts

explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning splits the word as DE-SPOT; absolute echoes Lord Acton's line that absolute power corrupts absolutely.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant ruling with unlimited power is a despot, and taking spots off something would de-spot it.

clue.text: Not a 19 one of the L8!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: 19 is LITTLE, and not a little is a lot
second meaning: ... the Miller's Son, one of Robin Hood's outlaws

explanation.walkthrough: The L8 are the Lincoln green men, Robin Hood's band; Much the Miller's Son is one of its lesser-known members.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposite of a little amount is a large quantity, and Much is the miller's son in the Robin Hood ballads.

clue.text: Meandering writer can dry up round the edges

indicators.note: one word wrapped round others forms their edges, enclosing them

parts.note: sere means dried up or withered
a pen is a writing instrument
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: An author whose ink can dry up around the edges of the page.
explanation.walkthrough: Writer suggests a person, but it is the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Serpentine means winding like a snake, so a serpentine river or road is meandering.

clue.text: See 24
A youngster on ascent outside mine from down under

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down entry an ascent reads upwards, so the letters run from bottom to top

parts.note: a lad is a youngster

indicators.note: a word placed outside another surrounds it

parts.note: taken as written
a pit is a mine

explanation.surface: A young man climbing out of an Australian mine.
explanation.walkthrough: The ascent applies to everything after the first A, not just the youngster: the boy and the surrounded mine are read upwards together.
explanation.definitionFit: The antipodes are Australia and New Zealand, on the opposite side of the globe from Britain, so antipodal means from down under.

clue.text: One of the L8 to plunder incognito?

parts.note: to rob is to plunder
someone in a hood is disguised

explanation.surface: One of the band sets out to steal while disguised.
explanation.walkthrough: The L8 are the Lincoln green men, after the cloth Robin Hood's outlaws wore.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood is the leader of the legendary outlaw band of Sherwood, so he counts among its members.

clue.text: Agitated male sheep

parts.note: he is a male
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A ram that is all worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: Male sheep reads as one phrase for a ram; it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Het up is an informal British phrase for flustered or worked up, a state of excitement or anger.

clue.text: Ayesha's quashed half the rabble from 13, enemy of L8

indicators.note: quashing half of a word suppresses that portion, so only the other half remains

parts.note: Ayesha is She-who-must-be-obeyed in H. Rider Haggard's novel She
riff-raff is the rabble

explanation.surface: A formidable woman has crushed half the mob.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is NOTTINGHAM, so this is the Sheriff of Nottingham.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sheriff of Nottingham is Robin Hood's chief foe, forever trying to catch the outlaws of Sherwood.

clue.text: Radiant essayist visiting hospital department

parts.note: Charles Lamb, author of the Essays of Elia
the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A glowing writer pays a call on a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: Visiting only puts the writer next to the department, not inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambent describes light that glows softly or flickers over a surface, so it means radiant or gently shining.
